The '''2024 United States Senate election in West Virginia''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[West Virginia|State of West Virginia]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Jim Justice]] won his first term in office, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Wheeling mayor Glenn Elliott. He succeeded [[Independent politician|independent]] incumbent [[Joe Manchin]], who did not seek a third full term.<ref name="retire">{{cite news |last1=Weaver |first1=Al |date=November 9, 2023 |title=Manchin won't seek reelection in West Virginia |work=The Hill |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/4302658-manchin-wont-seek-reelection-in-west-virginia/ |url-status=live |access-date=November 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109194551/https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/4302658-manchin-wont-seek-reelection-in-west-virginia/ |archive-date=November 9, 2023}}</ref>

Manchin, a Democrat until his final year in the Senate, announced he would not run for re-election shortly before switching to independent.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fortinsky |first=Kathryn |date=May 31, 2024 |title=Sen. Joe Manchin leaves Democratic Party, registers as an independent |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/democrat-joe-manchin-registers-independent/ |access-date=May 31, 2024 |newspaper=CBS News}}</ref> He endorsed Elliott, who won the Democratic nomination with 45% of the vote against political activist Zach Shrewsbury and businessman [[Don Blankenship]]. Justice won the Republican nomination with 62% of the vote against Congressman [[Alex Mooney]].

Due to West Virginia's heavy Republican lean, the absence of Manchin, Justice's personal popularity, and being held concurrently with a [[2024 United States presidential election|presidential race]] in a state in which [[Donald Trump]] was expected to win in a landslide, a Republican pickup for this seat was considered a foregone conclusion in 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Jessica |title=With Manchin Retirement, Democratic-Held Seat Moves to Solid Republican |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/senate/west-virginia-senate/manchin-retirement-democratic-held-seat-moves-solid-republican |access-date=June 5, 2025 |work=The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter |date=November 9, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Inside Elections" /><ref name="Decision Desk HQ/The Hill" /><ref name="Sabato's Crystal Ball" /><ref name="auto2"/>  Justice was sworn in as a Senator on January 14, 2025, giving elected Republicans control of both of West Virginia’s Senate seats for the first time since 1931 and giving the state an entirely Republican congressional delegation for the first time since 1923.{{efn|Republicans held both of West Virginia's Senate seats in 1958 when Republican [[John Hoblitzell]] was appointed to continue the term of Democrat [[Matthew M. Neely]] before losing his bid to finish Neely's term in a [[1958 United States Senate special election in West Virginia|special election the same year]].}} This was the first time since the [[1956 United States Senate special election in West Virginia|1956 special election]] that a Republican won West Virginia's Class I Senate Seat.

==Background==
Manchin saw electoral success through the 2010s, positioning himself as a [[Centrism|centrist]] to [[Conservatism|conservative]] Democrat with strong ties to West Virginia,<ref>{{Cite news|last=Edmondson|first=Catie|date=October 8, 2018|title=Joe Manchin's Yes on Kavanaugh Finds Sympathy in West Virginia (Published 2018)|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/10/08/us/politics/joe-manchin-brett-kavanaugh-west-virginia.html|access-date=January 10, 2021|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=June 16, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616092233/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/10/08/us/politics/joe-manchin-brett-kavanaugh-west-virginia.html|url-status=live}}</ref> which is now considered a [[Red states and blue states|deeply red]] state at the federal and state levels.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Chinni|first1=Dante|last2=Rivera|first2=Matt|date=December 18, 2016|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/meet-the-press/west-virginia-how-bluest-state-became-reddest-n697491|title=West Virginia: How the Bluest State Became the Reddest|location=[[Charleston, West Virginia]]|publisher=[[NBC News]]|access-date=October 27, 2026}}</ref>

The Republican Party identified this contest as a top priority in the 2024 election cycle.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Everett |first=Burgess |date=August 2, 2022 |title=GOP eyes 2024 payback for Manchin's Dems-only deal |language=en |website=POLITICO |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/08/02/manchin-republicans-reelection-00049135 |access-date=October 10, 2022 |archive-date=August 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806040947/https://www.politico.com/news/2022/08/02/manchin-republicans-reelection-00049135 |url-status=live }}</ref> Amongst the Republicans who ran for this seat were Congressman [[Alex Mooney]]<ref name=":0" /> and Governor [[Jim Justice]].<ref name=":1" />

Due to the state's heavy partisan lean, the narrow margin by which Manchin was re-elected in [[2018 United States Senate election in West Virginia|2018]], and a likely strong Republican presidential performance on the same ballot, Republicans were favored to win this seat even if Manchin sought re-election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kondik |first=Kyle |title=Initial Senate Ratings: Democrats Have a Lot of Defending to Do – Sabato's Crystal Ball |date=January 24, 2023 |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/initial-senate-ratings-democrats-have-a-lot-of-defending-to-do/ |access-date=January 25, 2023 |language=en-US |archive-date=January 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130223855/https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/initial-senate-ratings-democrats-have-a-lot-of-defending-to-do/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After Justice announced his bid for the seat in April 2023, ''Elections Daily'' labeled this race as "Safe Republican" due to his strong polling advantage against Manchin.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |last=Cunningham |first=Eric |date=May 4, 2023 |title=Jim Justice's Announcement Moves West Virginia's Senate Race to Safe Republican |url=https://elections-daily.com/2023/05/04/jim-justices-announcement-moves-west-virginias-senate-race-to-safe-republican/ |access-date=May 4, 2023 |website=Elections Daily |language=en-US |archive-date=May 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230521033048/https://elections-daily.com/2023/05/04/jim-justices-announcement-moves-west-virginias-senate-race-to-safe-republican/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After Manchin announced his retirement, all major outlets rated this seat as an expected easy flip to GOP control. While some Democratic sources hoped that a primary victory by [[Don Blankenship]] would spur Manchin to run as an [[Independent politician|independent]], Manchin himself described that notion as a "long, long, long-shot scenario" that ended when Blankenship lost the primary.<ref name="indie">{{Cite news|last=Raju |first=Manu |date=March 14, 2024 |title=Schumer discusses 'long-shot scenario' with Manchin: Last-ditch Senate run in West Virginia |work=CNN |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/03/14/politics/joe-manchin-independent-senate-run/index.html |access-date=March 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314211642/https://edition.cnn.com/2024/03/14/politics/joe-manchin-independent-senate-run/index.html|archive-date=March 14, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>
